entities.summary: Achille Le Tonnelier de Breteuil (1781–1864) was a French politician who played a significant role in the French Revolution. He was a key figure in the National Assembly and served as a member of the Chamber of Deputies. De Breteuil was a strong advocate for the rights of the common people and worked to establish a more equitable society. He was a key negotiator in the Treaty of Paris, which ended the French Revolutionary Wars and marked the beginning of the Napoleonic era. De Breteuil's legacy continues to be felt in modern France, where his emphasis on social justice and equality remains an important part of the country's values. The French Revolution's impact on European history cannot be overstated, and de Breteuil's contributions were a crucial factor in shaping the course of events.
